question: True or false: the rise in American mortgage defaults after 2007 was concentrated among low-income borrowers?
answer: False. Adelino, Schoar and Severino found defaults rose across all incomes and credit scores, and the share owed by middle-income, high-income and prime borrowers jumped. Subprime loans failed at higher rates, but prime loans were far more numerous, so a lower rate on a bigger base supplied much of the losses.
move: A modest rate across many can outweigh a high rate among few.
trap: Equating the group with the worst default rate with most defaults.
